about: This piece belongs to the formulary of the First Sunday of Advent, which opens the liturgical year in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s01.translation: To You, O God, I lift up my soul. In You I trust. Let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies exult over me, for none who await You shall be put to shame.

s02.translation: Make Your ways known to me, O Lord, and teach me Your paths.

s03.translation: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

s04.narrative: After the doxology the priest repeats the Introit antiphon from Ad te levávi to the psalm verse.

s05.translation: To You, O God, I lift up my soul. In You I trust. Let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies exult over me, for none who await You shall be put to shame.

w012.gloss: may I be put to shame
w012.function: The form is formally either future indicative or present subjunctive. The psalm's parallel future and its petitionary sense do not settle the morphology, so tense and mood are left unclaimed.

w017.function: A masculine nominative plural agreeing with “inimíci” (w016).

w019.function: The adjective stands substantivally for all people. Its relative clause identifies them as those who await the Lord.

w035.function: The doxology has no expressed verb. It supplies the wish “glory be” from liturgical usage.
